A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DGS/Fisher-information exploration system, with a substantial LLM extension in v2. The main text, equations and tables support comparison. However, v2 Figure 8 has a blank depth panel and embedded RMSE/coverage panels positioned outside the page, limiting comparison of those appendix results.

before.justification: V1 reports original Habitat simulation results on Gibson and HM3D, including reconstruction, tracking, coverage and a localization-uncertainty ablation in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulation results for the revised system, component ablations involving the LLM and localization uncertainty, and quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

M1.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o as a long-horizon planner using annotated bird’s-eye renderings and contextual prompts to select frontier targets or request refinement of explored space. Candidate-pose generation follows that selection instead of v1’s heuristic frontier selection. The Fisher-information path objective and Gaussian SLAM backbone are substantially retained.

E1.justification: The appendices identify the same nine Gibson scenes and five HM3D scenes. Both versions evaluate indoor exploration, reconstruction and localization with the same planar robot action space. The added LLM and HM3D rendering examples do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables retain the same comparators: ANS, Active-INR (gt), UPEN (gt), UPEN, ExplORB and FBE on Gibson; UPEN (gt), UPEN and FBE on HM3D. Newly discussed foundation-model methods and NARUTO are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 drops percentage coverage as an evaluation metric while retaining area coverage and the common 2000-step, 800×800 RGB-D protocol. Its replacement ablation is labeled HM3D in Table 3, although the prose still says Gibson. Appendix A.2 additionally states η=0.2 while retaining η=5, so the actual weight used is unresolved.

E4.justification: V1’s two-condition localization ablation on Gibson is replaced by three conditions: without LLM and localization uncertainty, without LLM, and the full system. This substantially extends the component analysis to the new planner, although v2 inconsistently identifies the ablation dataset. Appendix A.5 also adds an illustrative LLM planning interaction.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Fisher-based localization uncertainty remains part of the method rather than statistical uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace the proposed system’s result rows. Gibson PSNR/LPIPS change from 23.08/0.1794 to 23.28/0.2507; HM3D changes from 18.74/0.3534 to 19.86/0.4122. These describe different system versions, not controlled same-method improvements. FBE’s Gibson ATE changes from 0.0168 to 0.1680. Percentage-coverage results disappear, new component results and HM3D test renderings appear, and v2 no longer has the best LPIPS in either main table. The damaged appendix display limits some per-scene comparisons.

T1.justification: The central Fisher-information, EIG and Cramér–Rao reasoning is retained. V2 Appendix A.1 adds explicit skew-matrix expressions for pose Jacobians and changes the documented rendering formulation to transmittance/density expressions, while v1’s explicit projection and chain-rule equations are no longer supplied in that form. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the contribution from Fisher-based active Gaussian SLAM to a two-stage system combining zero-shot LLM planning with uncertainty-aware geometric planning. LLM use becomes a central claimed contribution, and the novelty statement is reframed around active mapping without ground-truth camera poses.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantial explanations of complementary semantic and geometric planning, scene-layout priors and avoiding infeasible destinations. It replaces v1’s percentage-coverage/localization tradeoff discussion with an interpretation of LLM effects. However, its statement that adding the LLM increases ATE contradicts Table 3, where ATE decreases from 0.1694 to 0.0336. The existing 3DOF applicability boundary remains.

D1.justification: V2 documents GPT-4o, the complete prompt, contextual image annotations and the JSON target interface in Section 3.2 and Appendix A.5. It also adds CUDA implementation information, an Nvidia L40 timing of 30 frames per second for Fisher computation, and λ=10^-6. Reproducibility is complicated by conflicting η values and the retained heuristic frontier-selection instructions alongside the new LLM procedure. Both PDFs still promise a future code release.

R1.justification: V2 introduces a substantial foundation-model planning literature discussion, including MapGPT, PaLM-E, VoxPoser, SayPlan, LLM-Planner and VLFM. It also adds positioning against NARUTO and replaces much of v1’s detailed visual-SLAM lineage discussion. This changes the research framing beyond citation renumbering or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around LLM-guided active mapping. The method gains a separate long-horizon planning section, preliminary material is reorganized, and the appendix expands from implementation/results sections to five subsections including background and prompting.

P2.justification: V2 changes the manuscript from one-column to two-column layout, redraws the pipeline with an LLM stage, adds interaction illustrations and HM3D test renderings, and restructures tables and metric plots. Existing reconstruction comparisons are resized and repeated at larger size in the appendix. Figure 8 also introduces a substantial display defect: a blank depth panel pushes subsequent panels and the caption outside the page.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a substantive LLM planner, component evidence and useful prompt/runtime documentation. These gains coexist with new reporting and reproducibility problems: Table 3 conflicts with its discussion about the dataset and ATE trend, Appendix A.2 gives incompatible weights and frontier-selection descriptions, and the retained all-metrics superiority claim contradicts the LPIPS results. The damaged HM3D appendix figure further reduces inspectability. The added contribution and these material regressions leave the net change in overall paper quality uncertain.
